back: Female XX, male XY; the sperm (X or Y) decides the sex of a child.
Inheritance of a characteristic controlled by a gene on a sex chromosome (usually X), so the pattern differs between sexes.
A heterozygous female ($X^H X^h$) who does not show a recessive condition but can pass on the allele.

front: Why are males more often affected by X-linked recessive conditions?
back: They have one X (hemizygous); one recessive allele is expressed. Females need two.
Children: 1/4 affected; sons: 1/2 affected; daughters: 1/2 carriers.

front: Can an affected father pass an X-linked condition to his son?
back: No: sons receive his Y. All his daughters receive his X and are at least carriers.
Superscript on X only: $X^H X^h$, $X^h Y$; never write an allele on the Y.

front: Two X-linked recessive conditions to know
back: Haemophilia (F8, factor VIII) and red-green colour blindness.

front: Pedigree signs of X-linked recessive inheritance
back: More affected males; carrier mothers; no father-to-son transmission; skips generations.
